newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF REAL MADRID PLAYERS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-PEN PICTURES OF REAL MADRID PLAYERS.

text.p: Pen pictures of Real Madrid players most likely to play in Saturday's Spanish league match against Atletico Madrid in the Vicente Calderon stadium:

Bodo Illgner, goalkeeper, 29. A surprise signing at the beginning of the season after manager Fabio Capello demanded a taller keeper, the former German international has become one of the mainstays of the Real side since ousting Canizares and veteran Paco Buyo.

Santiago Canizares, goalkeeper, 27. Shot to prominence after keeping Spain's World Cup hopes alive against Denmark in 1993, Canizares has played second fiddle to Buyo and then to Illgner since joining Real from Celta Vigo.
Rafael Alkorta, defender, 28. A regular in the national side and ever-present at the heart of the Real defence this season, Alkorta is one of the toughest markers in Spain.
Fernando Hierro, defender, 28. The tower on which the Real defence is built, Hierro comes forward well and is strong in the air at set-pieces. A potentially lethal free-kick specialist.
Chendo Porlan, defender 35. Veteran defender who has been playing for Real since 1983. Chendo is an unlikely starter but always a reliable substitute.
Roberto Carlos, defender, 23. Lighting quick in turning defence into attack down the left, the Brazilian international is a fine corner taker and has a devastating shot at set-pieces.

Carlos Secretario, defender 26. Right-sided Portuguese international defender, Secretario has been heavily criticised for his sluggishness since joining from Oporto in the close season. Has suffered from comparisons with Roberto Carlos.
Christian Panucci, defender, 23. Likely to make his debut in Secretario's place on the right of defence after signing from AC Milan for around 700 million pesetas ($5.34 million) last week.
Fernando Sanz, defender, 23. Substitute defender who is still trying to escape the shadow of being the son of Real president Lorenzo Sanz.
Luis Milla, midfielder, 30. Milla's signing from Barcelona sent shock-waves through the Spanish game back in 1990. However, Milla has since fallen from favour and is an unlikely starter.
Manuel Sanchis, midfielder, 31. Son of another Real star, Sanchis had been a regular first-team choice in both defence and midfield since 1993 but has struggled to impress Capello.
Fernando Redondo, midfielder, 27. Argentine international with a delicate touch, the injury-prone Redondo has yet to find his form this season after missing seven months league action.
Clarence Seedorf, midfielder, 20. Dutch international whose busy support work behind the front men has made him an unsung hero since signing from Ajax in the close season.
Victor Sanchez, midfielder, 20. Quietly efficient midfielder whose work down the right has earned him promotion from Real's B team. Played a superb game against Barcelona last month.
Emilio Amavisca, midfielder/striker, 25. A skilful support player rather than goalscorer, the Spanish international has recently returned after missing several months through injury.

Raul Gonzalez, midfielder/striker, 19. Became an instant first choice aged just 17 and continues to improve despite playing out of position after being moved back to the left side of midfield with the arrival of Suker and Mijatovic.

Davor Suker, striker, 29. With 14 goals already this season the Croatian Euro 96 star has continued to shine since signing from Sevilla. Heavily left-sided, Suker can take on men and beat them before unleashing a powerful shot. Strong at set-pieces.
Predrag Mijatovic, striker, 27. The Montenegrin's lethal right foot made him Spain's second-highest goalscorer at Valencia last season. Frequently accused of diving in the penalty area.
